outcome: No resolution, partial case, or bound extension found since 26 January 2024; the only two known Wolstenholme primes (16843, 2124679) and the >10^11 search bound (Booker, Hathi, Mossinghoff, Trudgian, 2022) are unchanged, and even a hypothetical new bound extension would not count under the scope rule for infinitude questions (§3.1).
summary: This bullet asks whether there are infinitely many Wolstenholme primes (primes p with C(2p-1,p-1) ≡ 1 mod p^4, a strengthening of Wolstenholme's theorem, which ordinarily holds only mod p^3). Only two are known — 16843 and 2124679 — and McIntosh's 1995 conjecture that infinitely many exist remains unproved. The most recent substantive computational result is Booker, Hathi, Mossinghoff and Trudgian's 2022 Ramanujan Journal paper 'Wolstenholme and Vandiver primes,' which extended the search bound to 10^11 (60 billion, per one summary) and predates the frozen revision, so it is not itself an in-window event; I found no successor paper extending this bound further in the 2024-2026 window. The current Wikipedia article, the Prime Pages glossary (t5k.org), and OEIS A088164 all still report only the same two known primes and the same pre-2024 bound, with the only 2025 OEIS edit (Thomas Ordowski, April 2025) being a cosmetic alternative characterization (a tanh/artanh identity equivalent to the existing congruence), not a mathematical advance. I also found a real but out-of-scope 2026 arXiv paper (Alexandre Linhares, 'Deep Vision: A Formal Proof of Wolstenholme's Theorem in Lean 4,' arXiv:2604.16507, submitted 14 April 2026) reporting an AI-assisted ('relational analogy engine') Lean 4 formalization of Wolstenholme's theorem itself — the classical 1862 congruence true for all primes p≥5 mod p^3, not the rare mod-p^4 Wolstenholme primes this bullet is about. Per §3.1 this is a related result sharing a name/topic, not a case of this problem, since it says nothing about the existence or count of Wolstenholme primes; I also note that even a genuine new search-bound extension would not count as movement on this bullet, since per the triage rules an infinitude/existence question is only settled by an actual proof, not by narrowing where a counterexample-type object could hide. No search turned up any 2024-2026 work claiming progress toward, or a proof of, the infinitude conjecture itself. Status is therefore 'open' with no_change_found true, matching the triage's 'none' verdict, which I confirm rather than dispute.
competing_reading: One could argue the Linhares Lean 4 paper is adjacent enough (same theorem family, same 'Wolstenholme' name, uses AI) to be worth flagging as AI activity in the surrounding topic area, and a looser reader might conflate 'Wolstenholme's theorem' with 'Wolstenholme primes' as one search snippet did. But the bullet is specifically about the existence of infinitely many primes satisfying the stronger mod-p^4 congruence, and the Linhares paper neither states nor implies anything about that count; it formalizes the universal theorem that already held for all primes since 1862. I judge this to be a related/namesake result, not a case of the problem, and coded it as no AI involvement in this record's outcome.
what_would_settle_it: A paper or preprint (i) proving infinitude of Wolstenholme primes, or (ii) at minimum extending the computational search past 10^11 with a stated new bound, dated after 26 January 2024, from a source such as arXiv, the Ramanujan Journal, Mathematics of Computation, or an update to OEIS A088164/t5k.org reporting a change in the known bound or a third example.
